metadata.name: payvand
metadata.description: On-chain payment records for Payvand QR payments

instructions.name: close_budget
docs: Reclaim whatever is left in the budget and retire it. One wallet
signature: the pot and the account's rent go back to the buyer, less the
network fee. The session key's fee float is not this account's money — a
PDA cannot move lamports off a plain keypair — so the client sweeps it
from the device that holds the key.

instructions.name: close_token_budget
docs: Drain the token vault back to the buyer and retire the budget. One
wallet signature: the tokens come back, and so do the vault's rent and
the budget account's rent. The session key's float is swept by the
client, as in `close_budget`.

accounts.name: mint
docs: only to refuse a Token-2022 mint by name, as on the other token contexts.

accounts.name: vault
docs: The canonical vault, as in `pay_from_token_budget`, so a decoy account
that shares the mint and the budget's authority cannot be drained in its
place.

instructions.name: initialize_config
docs: Creates the singleton fee policy. Callable once, by the program's
upgrade authority, which becomes the admin — so no caller can install
an admin of its choosing.

accounts.name: admin
docs: The upgrade authority: pays for `Config` and becomes its admin.

accounts.name: program_data
docs: upgradeable loader's PDA for this program id and the owner check pins it
to that loader, so a decoy account cannot stand in for it. The handler
reads the upgrade authority out of it.

accounts.name: treasury
docs: The fee destination. Created outside this instruction (it needs no data
and no signature), and pinned here by its seed.

instructions.name: migrate_config
docs: Upgrades the live config account — version 1, 2 or 3 — to version 4 in
place. Admin only, and only once: the account must be one of the older
layouts and must record the signer as its admin. It carries the admin, fee
mode and session float over and installs the `FeePolicy` passed here,
except the four price-derived fields — both token flats and the network
fee's two token equivalents — which it zeroes until
`set_fee_price_anchor` prices them.

accounts.name: admin
docs: The recorded admin. Pays the rent the taller account now needs.

accounts.name: config
docs: seeds derive it, and the handler checks its owner, its length and that
the admin it records is the signer before touching it.

instructions.name: open_budget
docs: Buyer funds this month's spending budget and registers a session key.
This is the ONE wallet signature the whole feature needs: afterwards
the session key — an app-generated keypair stored on the device — can
settle invoices from the pot without touching the wallet again.

accounts.name: buyer
docs: Main wallet: the one signature the buyer ever makes.

accounts.name: session_key
docs: the only key allowed to spend from the budget afterwards.

accounts.name: config
docs: Supplies the session float, so a policy change reaches every new budget.

instructions.name: open_token_budget
docs: Buyer opens (or tops up) this month's budget for one token and
registers a session key for it. One wallet signature per token; after
that the session key settles token invoices from the vault without
touching the wallet again.

accounts.name: mint
docs: a Token-2022 mint by name, as on the other token contexts.

accounts.name: buyer_token_account
docs: Where the budget's tokens come from — the buyer's own account.

accounts.name: vault
docs: The pot itself: a token account owned by the budget PDA, so only this
program can ever move what is inside it.

accounts.name: session_key
docs: the only key allowed to spend from this budget afterwards.

instructions.name: open_treasury_token_account
docs: Opens the treasury's own token account for a mint, paid by the admin.
A mint the treasury has no account for cannot be settled: the fee has
nowhere to go, and the buyer would only find out after signing. Run this
once for every mint the app can price in, before its first invoice.

accounts.name: admin
docs: Pays the account's rent. The treasury's own lamports are the pool the
fee is measured against, so they are not spent on accounts.

accounts.name: mint
docs: refuse a Token-2022 mint by name; the ATA program still proves it is a
mint when the account is created.

accounts.name: treasury_token_account
docs: The fee's destination in this mint: the treasury's own account, created
here when it is missing and left alone when it is not.

instructions.name: pay_from_budget
docs: Silent payment: the session key settles an invoice straight out of the
buyer's budget — no wallet popup, because the only signature here is
the local session key's. The pot pays the seller and refunds the invoice
rent, the marker's rent and the network fee the session key advanced from
its float.
The monthly cap and the pot balance are both enforced here, and the
amount still rides in the payment PDA's seeds, so a QR code can only
ever be settled for exactly the price it shows — the same guarantee
`settle_payment` gives.

accounts.name: session_key
docs: Session key: fee payer and rent payer (made whole by the pot in this
same transaction). Never the buyer's wallet.

accounts.name: seller
docs: allowed to receive the lamports.

accounts.name: receipt
docs: The permanent marker; `settled_at` is the replay guard. The session key
advances its rent and the pot reimburses it, so the seller carries the
cost through the reduced proceeds.

accounts.name: reference
docs: seed and an address watchers can look up.

accounts.name: config
docs: The fee policy. Read-only here.

accounts.name: treasury
docs: The fee destination, pinned by seed.

instructions.name: pay_from_token_budget
docs: Silent token payment: the session key settles a token invoice out of
the buyer's vault, with no wallet popup. The monthly cap, the vault
balance and the amount in the invoice seeds are all enforced here, and
only the session key registered at open time may spend.
The price pays everything: the seller receives it less the fee, the fee
lands in the treasury's own account for the mint, and the pool refunds the
two rents the session key advanced and takes the closed invoice's rent
back. The vault therefore falls by exactly the price, and the seller
receives no lamports at all.

accounts.name: session_key
docs: Session key: fee payer and rent payer (refunded from the pool in this
same transaction). Never the buyer's wallet.

accounts.name: vault
docs: The canonical vault and the only accepted one: the budget's associated
token account for this mint. A token account that merely shares the mint
and the budget's authority is a place to strand a budget's tokens, so it
is not a vault.

accounts.name: mint
docs: the currency policy, and the rejection is named: `Token2022Unsupported`.

accounts.name: seller
docs: less the fee in tokens and no lamports — the invoice's rent goes back to
the pool that advanced it.

accounts.name: seller_token_account
docs: The seller's own token account, which must already exist — the same rule
`settle_token_payment` applies. Creating it here would spend the session
float, and that float is the buyer's money: the rent would be a fee the
buyer pays, and nobody refunds it. Opening the account is the seller's
setup step, like having a wallet at all.

accounts.name: config
docs: The fee policy: the rate this payment pays and the treasury's bump.
Read-only here, as on the other two settle paths.

accounts.name: treasury
docs: The SOL pool: it refunds the rents the session key advanced and receives
the invoice rent back when the invoice closes, so the pot pays the price
and the seller keeps the price less the fee.

accounts.name: treasury_token_account
docs: The fee's destination in this mint, opened once per mint by whoever runs
the treasury — the same account `settle_token_payment` pays.

instructions.name: refresh_fee_price
docs: Re-pegs the two token flats — the marker's rent expressed in USDC and in
EURC — and the network fee's two token equivalents to a live SOL price.
Permissionless and bounded: a plausible price only, one within
`PRICE_ANCHOR_BAND_BPS` of the admin's anchor, and one call a minute. The
band is measured from the anchor rather than the flat it rewrites, so
repeated calls cannot walk the flats anywhere.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Anyone may call this and pays the network fee for it; the bounds inside
are the protection, not the key. The app refreshes the flats from its
rate feed on the same five-minute cache it prices invoices with.

accounts.name: anchor
docs: The admin's price the supplied one is measured against. Required rather
than optional: a deployment whose admin has not priced it yet has no
band, so there is nothing to refresh within.

instructions.name: set_fee_price_anchor
docs: Writes the SOL price the permissionless refresh is measured against —
`["fee-anchor"]`, created on the first call — and prices both token flats
at it from the cluster's current rent. Admin only: it is the one price a
permissionless caller cannot choose.

accounts.name: admin
docs: The recorded admin: the only key whose price the band is measured from.

accounts.name: anchor
docs: Created on the first call and rewritten on every later one.

instructions.name: settle_payment
docs: Buyer pays an invoice. The invoice account is created inside this same
transaction, so the seller never has to sign anything to open a payment
code — the QR is just an address plus its details.
The buyer spends the price and nothing else: a `sponsor` advances the two
records and pays the transaction's fee, and the price repays it in this
same instruction. A funded wallet is its own sponsor; a wallet holding no
SOL passes a relayer's key, which is what makes a SOL invoice payable by
someone who cannot afford a signature.
`amount` is part of the PDA seeds, which is what keeps this safe: an
invoice can only ever be settled at the exact amount that was encoded
into the QR code, because any other amount derives a different account
address than the one the seller is watching.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Pays the price and nothing else. It owns no lamports beyond the invoice:
the two records are the sponsor's to advance and the network fee is the
sponsor's to pay, so a wallet holding exactly the price can settle.

accounts.name: payment
docs: Short-lived: created, settled and closed in this one transaction. Its
rent is advanced by the sponsor and returns to the seller when the
account closes, who fronts no signature for it.

accounts.name: seller
docs: account allowed to receive the lamports.

accounts.name: receipt
docs: The permanent marker. `settled_at != 0` means this invoice is done, so
the same invoice can never be settled twice. The sponsor fronts its rent
and the price repays it, so the seller is the one who ends up paying for
the record.

accounts.name: reference
docs: used as a PDA seed and as an address that watchers can look up.

accounts.name: config
docs: The fee policy. Read-only here: only the admin writes it.

accounts.name: treasury
docs: The fee destination, pinned by seed so the payer cannot name another
account. Nothing else about a SOL settlement touches it.

accounts.name: sponsor
docs: Who fronts what the payment costs in lamports: the invoice's rent, the
marker's rent and the transaction's own fee. It receives both rents back
plus `network_fee_lamports` out of the price in this same instruction, so
its net cost is the fee it paid and nothing else. A funded wallet passes
itself — one key, one signature — and a wallet holding no SOL passes a
relayer's key, which turns a payer who cannot afford a signature into a
payer without renting it the rest.
Required rather than optional: an absent sponsor would have to mean the
payer fronts the records, which is the cost this account exists to move
off the payer.

instructions.name: settle_token_payment
docs: Buyer pays a token-denominated invoice straight from their wallet.
Same guarantee as `settle_payment`: the amount rides in the PDA seeds,
so an invoice can only ever be settled for the exact price its QR
shows. The mint is in the seeds too, so a USDC invoice and a SOL
invoice that happen to share a reference and a price are different
accounts and cannot pay for each other.
The buyer signs for its own token account, and a `sponsor` pays for the
settlement's two record rents and receives the treasury's refund of
them. A funded wallet passes itself as the sponsor — one signature, no
change in cost — and a wallet holding only the token passes a relayer's
key, which turns a zero-lamport buyer into a payer without being a
lamport faucet for it.

accounts.name: payer
docs: The buyer. Its signature proves it owns `payer_token_account` — which is
all a sponsor cannot do for it — and its wallet loses nothing: every
lamport this settlement advances belongs to `sponsor` below.

accounts.name: seller
docs: through its own associated token account, checked below.

accounts.name: seller_token_account
docs: The seller's own token account, which must already exist. Creating one
here would mint rent to whoever named the seller, so opening it is the
seller's setup step — like having a wallet at all — and never a line on
the buyer's bill.

accounts.name: payer_token_account
docs: The same account as `seller_token_account` when the shop's owner is
paying their own invoice — one wallet, one account for the mint. Anchor
refuses two mutable accounts with one key unless the alias is named, and
the payout skips the seller's leg for exactly that case.

accounts.name: mint
docs: policy's currency rule, and the rejection is named: `Token2022Unsupported`
rather than a failure inside a token CPI.

accounts.name: reference
docs: and an address watchers can look up.

accounts.name: config
docs: The fee policy, read-only here. Same rules as the SOL path.

accounts.name: treasury
docs: The SOL pool: it refunds the rents the payer advanced and receives the
invoice rent back when the invoice closes.

accounts.name: treasury_token_account
docs: The fee's destination in this mint, opened once per mint by whoever runs
the treasury; the contract cannot create it without paying rent to a
seller's account, which is the faucet this avoids.

accounts.name: sponsor
docs: Who pays for this settlement's records. It advances the invoice's rent
and the marker's (`init`, above) and receives the treasury's refund of
both in this same instruction, so its net cost is the network fee — the
fee it signs as — and nothing else. A funded wallet passes its own key
here and is therefore its own sponsor; a wallet holding only the token
passes a relayer's, which turns a zero-lamport buyer into a payer.
The refund goes to this account and never to `payer` on purpose: a
sponsor that topped a buyer up would otherwise hand it both rents —
3,939,360 lamports per settlement at mainnet's rate — for the price of
one signature.

instructions.name: update_config
docs: Changes the fee policy. Admin only; it never rewrites `admin` itself.

instructions.name: withdraw_treasury
docs: Moves treasury surplus to the admin. It always leaves the account's
rent-exempt minimum plus `TREASURY_RESERVE_SETTLEMENTS` settlements' worth
of refunds, so a withdrawal cannot be what stops the next token payment.
No payment path can touch the treasury this way.

errors.msg: Payment amount must be greater than zero

errors.name: MemoTooLong
errors.msg: Memo exceeds the maximum length

errors.name: AlreadySettled
errors.msg: This payment has already been settled

errors.name: InvoiceTooSmall
errors.msg: This amount cannot cover the invoice account's rent

errors.name: InvalidSeller
errors.msg: The seller address is not valid

errors.name: BudgetExhausted
errors.msg: The monthly spending limit has been reached

errors.name: InsufficientBudget
errors.msg: The budget does not hold enough SOL for this payment

errors.name: InvalidSessionKey
errors.msg: The session key is not the one registered for this budget

errors.name: MintMismatch
errors.msg: The token does not match this budget

errors.name: ConfigMissing
errors.msg: This deployment has no fee config yet

errors.name: InvalidConfigAdmin
errors.msg: Only the program's upgrade authority may initialize the config

errors.name: ProgramNotUpgradeable
errors.msg: This program is not upgradeable, so it cannot bootstrap a config

errors.name: InvalidFeeBps
errors.msg: The fee rate cannot exceed 100%

errors.name: InvalidSessionFloat

errors.name: TreasuryUnderfunded
errors.msg: The treasury cannot cover the refund it owes

errors.name: FeeModeUnsupported
errors.msg: This fee mode is not supported yet

errors.name: FeeOverflow
errors.msg: The fee calculation overflowed

errors.name: Token2022Unsupported
errors.msg: Payvand settles only SPL Token mints; Token-2022 is not supported

errors.name: InvalidConfigVersion
errors.msg: This config account is not the version this migration upgrades

errors.name: InvalidFeePrice
errors.msg: That SOL price is not a price the program will write

errors.name: FeePriceTooSoon
errors.msg: The flats were refreshed a moment ago

errors.name: ShopFeeTooHigh
errors.msg: Retired: per-shop fee cap

errors.name: ShopPolicySellerMismatch

errors.name: InvalidNetworkFee
errors.msg: The network fee is larger than this program allows a policy to name

types.name: Budget
docs: The buyer's monthly spending pot: lamports held by the program plus the
rules that make the session key's signatures safe. Seeded by the buyer's
wallet, so there is exactly one per buyer.

fields.name: buyer
docs: Main wallet — funds, refills and closes the pot. The only wallet
that ever signs for this feature.

fields.name: session_key
docs: App-generated key allowed to spend from the pot without the wallet.

fields.name: monthly_limit
docs: Ceiling for one calendar month, in lamports.

fields.name: spent
docs: Spent so far in `month_index`.

fields.name: month_index
docs: `year * 12 + month` that `spent` belongs to; a new month resets it.

types.name: BudgetOpened
docs: A buyer opened or refilled an allowance. Same type for the SOL pot and a
token vault, with `mint` carrying the difference: `monthly_limit` is the
ceiling that now applies, and `session_key` is who may spend it.

fields.name: mint
docs: `Pubkey::default()` for the SOL budget.

types.name: Config
docs: The program's singleton fee policy and treasury pointers.
Created once per deployment by the program's upgrade authority, which
becomes `admin`. Settlements read it and never write it; only the admin can
change the policy, and the fee destination is derived from a seed here
rather than named by a caller, so no settlement can redirect it.
Version 4 carries the network fee beside the tiered `FeePolicy`; version 3 was
the same policy without it, version 2 without `flats_updated_at`, and version
1 one rate plus a flat lamport fee. `migrate_config` reallocates whichever it
finds.

fields.name: admin
docs: The upgrade authority that initialized the config. It may change the
policy and withdraw treasury surplus, nothing else.

fields.name: policy
docs: The two rates, their boundaries and the per-currency flats.

fields.name: fee_mode
docs: Who pays the fee.

fields.name: session_fee_float
docs: Lamports parked on a session key so its silent transactions can pay
their own network fees. Replaces the old hardcoded float.

fields.name: flats_updated_at
docs: When `policy`'s two token flats were last recomputed from a live SOL
price. Zero on a fresh or migrated config, so the first refresh is never
made to wait; `refresh_fee_price` sets it and refuses another within
`FLATS_REFRESH_SECS`.

types.name: ConfigUpdated
docs: The fee policy as the admin just wrote it, so an indexer prices a settlement
with the policy in force rather than today's. It carries the whole
`FeePolicy`, because a tiered fee needs both rates and both boundaries to be
reproduced.

types.name: FeeAnchor
docs: The SOL price the admin has blessed, in micros per SOL, for the two currencies
the flats are priced in.
`refresh_fee_price` is permissionless, so its band cannot be measured from the
flat it is about to rewrite: a caller could move that flat a band's worth
every cooldown, and a flat that drifts far enough from the rent stops covering
the receipt the treasury refunds, or overcharges a seller. The anchor is a
separate account the admin writes, so every permissionless refresh is bound to
the same price no matter how many of them ran before it.
It lives beside `Config` rather than inside it because it arrived after
version 3 was live: a new account needs no layout migration, and the app's
fixed-offset `Config` reader keeps working.

fields.name: sol_usd_micros
docs: The USD price of one SOL the admin last set, in micros.

fields.name: sol_eurc_micros
docs: The EUR price of one SOL, from the same decision.

types.name: FeePolicy
docs: The fee policy a `Config` carries: two marginal rates, the boundary they meet
at in each currency, and the flat each token currency pays for the marker's
rent.
The rate is marginal, not a cliff. An amount at or below the boundary pays
`fee_bps_below` on all of it; an amount above it pays `fee_bps_below` on the
part at or below the boundary plus `fee_bps_above` on the part above. A 0.1
SOL invoice and one lamport more therefore owe fees a lamport's worth of rate
apart, not twice as far.
The rates are also ceilinged: a fee never costs more than 0.1 SOL, 10 USDC or
10 EURC (`MAX_SOL_FEE_LAMPORTS` / `MAX_TOKEN_FEE_BASE_UNITS`), so the
percentage serves the everyday payment without letting a large invoice pay a
large multiple of what the service costs. The ceiling is the program's, not a
per-policy setting: no rate field raises it.
The two flat fields exist because a token settlement cannot charge its
non-signing seller lamports, so the treasury — not the seller — funds the
permanent marker's 1,224,960-lamport rent on that path. Charging the seller
that same cost in the currency they are paid in is what keeps the treasury
whole. `usdc_mint` and `eurc_mint` select them, and a mint that names neither
pays no flat.
The program has no oracle, so the flats cannot be derived at settle time.
They are instead kept *live*: `refresh_fee_price` recomputes both from the
cluster's current marker rent and a SOL price in micros, so what a token
seller is charged tracks what the record actually costs today rather than
what SOL was worth when the policy was written.
The network fee is the second cost a payment carries. Every settlement spends
one signature's worth of lamports, and on the token paths a sponsor advances
it; the treasury pays that sponsor back, and the seller pays the treasury the
same amount in the currency they were paid in. So the floor a token seller is
charged is the record's flat *plus* this fee, and the ceiling is the
percentage — the seller pays whichever is larger, never both. When the
percentage is the larger, it absorbs the two costs and what is left is the
protocol's revenue; when the costs are the larger, the protocol charges
nothing beyond them. The two token figures exist for the same reason the
flats do: a token amount cannot be priced in lamports without an oracle, so
they are derived from `refresh_fee_price`'s own SOL price like the flats.

fields.name: fee_bps_below
docs: Basis points on the part of the amount at or below the boundary.

fields.name: fee_bps_above
docs: Basis points on the part above it.

fields.name: sol_tier_lamports
docs: The SOL boundary, in lamports (100_000_000 = 0.1 SOL).

fields.name: token_tier_base_units
docs: The token boundary, in base units (10_000_000 = 10 USDC at 6 decimals).

fields.name: flat_usdc_base_units
docs: Flat charged on a USDC invoice, in base units: the marker's rent at the
SOL price the last `refresh_fee_price` wrote. A token settle charges the
larger of this and the percentage, so a small invoice pays the record
and nothing more.

fields.name: flat_eurc_base_units
docs: Flat charged on a EURC invoice, in base units, from the same refresh.

fields.name: usdc_mint
docs: The mint `flat_usdc_base_units` applies to.

fields.name: eurc_mint
docs: The mint `flat_eurc_base_units` applies to.

fields.name: network_fee_lamports
docs: What one settlement's network fee costs, in lamports: the amount the
treasury reimburses the account that paid the transaction's fee. A token
settle charges the seller this plus the record's rent, in the currency
they are paid in, and keeps the rest of the percentage.

fields.name: network_fee_usdc_base_units
docs: `network_fee_lamports` in USDC base units, from the same SOL price the
last `refresh_fee_price` wrote into the flats.

fields.name: network_fee_eurc_base_units
docs: `network_fee_lamports` in EURC base units, from the same refresh.

fields.name: reference
docs: Free-form lookup key chosen when the invoice was opened.

fields.name: amount
docs: Price in lamports.

fields.name: memo
docs: Human readable invoice note.

fields.name: payer
docs: Set once the invoice has been settled.

types.name: PaymentReceipt
docs: The permanent marker of a settled invoice — SOL or token.
The temporary `Payment`/`TokenPayment` account is created, settled and
closed inside one transaction; this marker is what survives, and it is
deliberately not a copy of the payment. Everything the payment was — the
split, the payer, the memo, the reference and the mint — is in the
`PaymentSettled` event that the same transaction logs, and the price and
memo are in the instruction data that produced it. Storing that again here
would cost the seller ~2.3 times the rent for a second copy of facts the
cluster already keeps.
What cannot move off chain is what only the runtime can answer:
- `settled_at` is the replay guard. A second settlement of the same invoice
finds this account already written and is refused with `AlreadySettled`,
atomically with the transfer rather than as a check made before it.
- `invoice` lets a program-wide scan (`get_program_accounts`) name the
invoice a marker belongs to. A PDA cannot be inverted, so without this a
scan sees an address and no way to say which payment it belongs to.
Its address is derived from the invoice address
(`["payment-receipt", invoice]`), so a watcher holding only the QR still
finds it with one derivation.

fields.name: invoice
docs: The invoice PDA this marker belongs to, so a program-wide scan can name
the invoice without a history read.

fields.name: settled_at
docs: Equal to the settle transaction's timestamp. Non-zero means this invoice
is done; zero is what `init_if_needed` leaves in a fresh account.

types.name: PaymentSettled
docs: One settled invoice — from the wallet path or an allowance, in SOL or a
token.
This event is the record. The permanent `PaymentReceipt` account keeps only
the replay guard and a pointer back to the invoice, so everything a ledger,
a seller's screen or the API needs to describe a settlement is here: it
lands in the same transaction, it cannot be rewritten, and it costs no rent.
All four settle instructions emit this same type, deliberately: `mint`
carries the currency (`Pubkey::default()` for SOL) and `payer` is whoever
signed, wallet or session key. `amount` is the price the QR showed, `fee` is
the seller's deduction above the marker's rent — on a token invoice the whole
of it, on SOL the part the rent does not already take — and
`seller_proceeds` is what the seller actually keeps: the price less the fee,
less the receipt rent where the seller carries it (the SOL paths; a token
seller is charged no lamports). `fee` is not revenue: the settlement first
pays the sponsor back the network fee it spent, and the treasury keeps what
is left.

fields.name: amount
docs: The invoice price, in lamports or the mint's base units.

fields.name: fee
docs: The seller's deduction above the marker's rent: the network fee the sponsor
is repaid plus the platform's margin.

fields.name: seller_proceeds
docs: `amount - fee` on a token settle, `amount - fee - receipt rent` on SOL:
the receipt rent is a cost the seller now carries, so the event states
the number after it rather than making every reader know the rule.

fields.name: payer
docs: Wallet or session key that settled.

fields.name: mint
docs: `Pubkey::default()` for a SOL invoice.

fields.name: reference
docs: The invoice's lookup key, as carried in its seeds.

fields.name: invoice
docs: The invoice PDA this settlement closed, so an indexer can key the payment
by the address the QR carries without re-deriving the seeds.

fields.name: memo
docs: The invoice note, which used to live in the receipt.

types.name: TokenBudget
docs: A buyer's monthly spending pot for one token: the vault holds the tokens
and this account holds the rules the session key's signatures obey.

fields.name: buyer
docs: Main wallet — funds, refills and closes the pot.

fields.name: session_key
docs: App-generated key allowed to spend from the vault without the wallet.

fields.name: mint
docs: The token this budget is denominated in.

fields.name: monthly_limit
docs: Ceiling for one calendar month, in the mint's base units.

fields.name: spent
docs: Spent so far in `month_index`.

fields.name: month_index
docs: `year * 12 + month` that `spent` belongs to.

types.name: TokenPayment
docs: An invoice paid in an SPL token. A separate account type from `Payment`
because it records the mint, and keeping it separate leaves every SOL
